sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
Tactical Command Wargame is a tactical tabletop wargame centered around battlefield positioning, command hierarchy, and strategic resource management.

Players do not directly control every soldier individually. Instead, they command Companies through Officers while directing the overall battle through a Commander.

Victory belongs to the player who best manages positioning, battlefield resources, and coordinated attacks.

sections.title: Core Philosophy
sections.body:
The game is built upon five pillars.

Command Wins Battles

Maintaining your command structure is more valuable than simply fielding stronger units.

Position Matters

Movement, flanking, terrain and formations determine victory more than dice rolls.

Tactical Simplicity

Individual units remain simple.

Strategic depth comes from:

Commanders

Officers

Positioning

Abilities

Company management

Reusable Abilities

Shared effects should be represented by reusable Passive (and Active) abilities whenever possible.

Abilities are defined once in the ability library rather than rewritten on every card.

Large Battles

The system is designed to comfortably support armies of approximately:

1 Commander

8 Officers

40 Combat Units

without excessive bookkeeping.

sections.title: Army Construction
sections.body:
Each player builds an army worth 200 Unit Value (UV).

A legal army contains:

Exactly 1 Commander

One or more Officers

Combat Units assigned to Officers

A player's army may never exceed 200 UV.

sections.title: Unit Value (UV)
sections.body:
Every card has a Unit Value.

The sum of all cards may not exceed the agreed army size.

Default game:

200 UV

sections.title: Commander
sections.body:
Each army contains exactly one Commander.

Commanders:

Generate Command Cost (CC)

Activate once each round

May move and fight

Have their own AP

Never spend CC to activate themselves

sections.title: Officers
sections.body:
Officers command Companies.

Each Officer possesses:

UV

Company UV Capacity

Company AP

Command Radius

Passive abilities

Activated abilities

Officers never generate CC.

sections.title: Combat Units
sections.body:
Combat Units belong to exactly one Company.

Combat Units remain assigned to that Company for the entire battle unless another rule changes this.

sections.title: Unit Types
sections.body:
There are three card types.

Commander

Leads the army.

Provides strategic abilities.

Generates CC.

Acts once each round.

Officer

Leads a Company.

Provides Company AP.

Supports nearby units.

Combat Unit

Forms the majority of the army.

Combat Units use Company AP instead of individual AP.

sections.title: Rarity
sections.body:
Rarity represents complexity and power budget.

It is not intended to represent collectible rarity.

Common

Black Gem

Usually:

Few or no abilities

Lower UV

Simple battlefield role

Uncommon

Silver Gem

Usually:

One or two abilities

Specialized battlefield role

Rare

Gold Gem

Usually:

Multiple abilities

Strong battlefield presence

Higher UV

More complex interactions

sections.title: Battlefield Setup
sections.body:
Players prepare the board and their armies in this order.

Setup Order

1. Commander placement

2. Objective placement

3. Terrain placement

4. Unit placement (Officers, then Companies)

Army Reveal (before or with step 1)

Reveal Commander, Officers, and Company assignments. Choose Deployed Units and Reserve Units (if the scenario allows).

1. Commander Placement

Each player places their Commander on their edge seat (or as the scenario directs).

Command Radius is measured from the Commander's hex for later terrain builds and Officer deploy.

Mark the Center

Mark the board's center hex (the mid hex of an odd-sized board, e.g. hex 17,17 on 35×35) with a permanent or reusable center reference token.

This center mark is not an objective unless an Objective Card says so. It exists so Objective Cards and terrain alignment stay easy to track at a glance.

2. Objective Placement

Objectives are placed using Objective Cards before any land or barrier terrain.

Objective Cards

Each Objective Card shows 1, 2, or 3 objective markers printed on a mini-map that aligns to the battlefield hex grid (same orientation as the board: edge seats N / W / S / E, and the center reference mark).

Cards with 1 objective are single contested points. Cards with 2 or 3 use pre-balanced spacing so no seat is systematically starved.

Draw Procedure

Shuffle the Objective Card deck.

Draw one card. That card is the layout for this game.

Align the card's center mark to the board's center reference, and its edge marks to N / W / S / E, then place objective markers on the matching hexes.

Optional: after drawing, roll for orientation — rotate the card 180° (or flip, if the card allows) so the same layout can face different seats without redrawing. Keep the centers aligned when rotating.

Do not draw a second card unless the scenario says otherwise.

Restrictions

Objective hexes are reserved: Water and Wall terrain may not be placed on them.

Fortified outlines and other passable terrain may sit adjacent to objectives, but must not replace the marker.

All markers from the drawn card are placed — you do not pick a subset.

Why cards

No player chooses VP sites, so placement stays fair. Variety comes from the deck (1 / 2 / 3 objectives and different geometries), not from freehand sitting.

3. Terrain Placement

Base board is Plains. Each player shapes their own Command Radius (CR) before deployment — either flood the entire CR with one terrain type, or place a fixed quota of pieces inside it.

Command Radius setup (choose one per player)

Flood: pick one terrain type and fill every hex in your CR with it (commander hex keeps soft land only if the type cannot cover commanders — Water never covers your commander hex).

Pieces: place shapes entirely inside your CR. Quota by player count:

- 2 players: 1 large + 2 medium + 2 small

- 4 players: 1 medium + 2 small (no large pieces)

Water appears only as small pieces. Same-kind overlap is allowed on a hex; different kinds cannot share a hex (exception: small land pieces may overwrite Water to create land bridges). Water/Wall may not seal your commander in or cut any commander off from objectives. Water and Wall may not be placed on objective hexes.

After all players finish CR terrain, remaining open hexes stay Plains and deployment begins.

Legacy note: older setups used shared neutral large/medium/small land drops after CR placement; the live client uses CR-only terrain.

Water and Walls cannot be placed on objective hexes. Objectives are always neutral land (Plains) for gameplay purposes — terrain may visually overlap an objective hex, but that hex remains passable neutral ground.

If a rolled or chosen piece would cover an objective with Water or Wall, it does not fit — use the failure ladder (smaller same type, then skip).

Land Bridges: Small land pieces (not medium or large) may be placed over existing water hexes inside your CR to create land bridges. This converts those water hexes to the land type being placed.

4. Unit Placement

Deployment follows the command chain.

Officers within Commander Radius (not on the outer Command Radius ring if that restriction is in use).

Units within Officer Radius.

No unit may begin Isolated.

Objective Distance

No unit (Officer or Combat Unit) may begin the game within 5 hexes of an objective marker.

Commanders are exempt from this 5-hex restriction if their edge seat would otherwise violate it (edge seats normally will not).

After setup, units may move freely toward objectives during play.

sections.title: Unit Statistics
sections.body:
Combat Units possess:

UV

Movement

Damage

Toughness

Range

Melee attacks always have Range 1 (shown as Melee).

Ranged attacks use printed Range 2–3.

Printed Range may never exceed 3. No unit prints Range 4 or higher as a base statistic.

Active abilities may grant temporary +Range (for example +1 Range this activation), which can raise effective Range above 3 for that effect only. Passives must not permanently raise printed Range above 3.

Temporary +Range is primarily an Elf tool (precision archery). Siege may use a narrow Siege-only elevation Active. Other factions should not freely access Range extension.

Abilities (if any)

Combat Units do not have AP.

Officer Statistics

Officers possess:

UV

Company UV Capacity

Company AP

Movement

Damage

Toughness

Range

Command Radius


Abilities

Commanders possess:

UV

CC Generation

AP

Movement

Damage

Range

Command Radius

sections.title: Company Structure
sections.body:
Every Officer commands exactly one Company.

Combat Units remain assigned to that Company.

Company UV Capacity

Every Officer has a Company UV Capacity.

The combined UV of assigned Combat Units may not exceed this value.

Example

Captain Rowan

Company UV Capacity: 24

Legal:

8 Spearmen (3 UV each)

Illegal:

5 Knights (6 UV each)

Company AP

Each Officer generates Company AP.

Company AP refreshes at the beginning of every round.

Most actions performed by a unit in that Company spend Company AP.

Examples include:

Attack

Brace

Evade

Retaliate

Activated abilities

Movement is free while the unit is inside its Officer's Command Radius. Movement costs Company AP only when the unit is outside Command Radius (including when Isolated).

Combat Units never possess individual AP.

Command Radius

A Company functions normally while its units remain inside the Officer's Command Radius.

Command Radius also determines which Combat Units benefit from Officer abilities. Officer Actives and Passives affect only Combat Units of that Officer's company (typically those in Command Radius), never units of other companies. Combat Unit abilities that target a friendly model (for example Heal) may affect any friendly creature within the ability's printed Range — Combat Units, Officers, or Commanders. Commander abilities may affect any model in that Commander's army (within the ability's printed Range or Command Radius).
Isolated Units

A unit becomes Isolated when it ends its activation outside its Officer's Command Radius.

Isolated units:

Remain members of their Company.

Still spend Company AP.

Cannot benefit from Officer abilities.

Every action costs +1 Company AP (Movement still only costs AP because the unit is outside Command Radius; Isolated adds the usual +1).

A unit is no longer Isolated once it begins an activation inside Command Radius again.

sections.title: Command System
sections.body:
Command is divided into two separate resources:

Command Cost (CC) represents strategic leadership and is generated by the Commander.

Company AP represents tactical execution and is generated by each Officer.

This separation minimizes bookkeeping while preserving tactical depth.

sections.title: Command Cost (CC)
sections.body:
CC is generated by the Commander at the start of every round.

Unused CC is lost at the end of the round unless another rule states otherwise.

CC is never used for standard movement or attacks.

sections.title: Spending CC
sections.body:
CC may only be spent to:

Activate an Officer.

Activate an Isolated Unit independently.

Temporarily promote a replacement Officer.

Resolve effects that explicitly require CC.

Unless specifically stated, Officers and Combat Units may never spend CC.

sections.title: Commander Activation
sections.body:
Each Commander activates once per round.

The Commander:

Does not spend CC to activate.

Generates and spends their own AP.

May move.

May attack.

May use Commander abilities.

Unless another rule states otherwise, a Commander may attack once per round.

sections.title: Turn Structure
sections.body:
Each round follows this sequence.

Phase 1 — Refresh

Generate Commander CC.

Refresh every Officer's Company AP.

Refresh Commander AP.

Resolve Start of Round effects.

Phase 2 — Initiative

Round One

Each player rolls a D6.

Highest roll chooses who activates first.

Re-roll ties.

Later Rounds

Initiative moves clockwise of the last initiative.

Phase 3 — Officer Activations

Players alternate activating Officers.

Each Officer activation costs CC.

Each Officer may activate once per round.

Continue until:

Both players pass consecutively, or

Neither player can legally activate another Officer.

Commander Activation (independent)

Each Commander activates once per round on their own track (no CC). This does not replace an Officer activation — the Commander may activate at any time during the round (before, between, or after Officers).

Phase 4 — End of Round

Resolve End of Round effects.

Remove temporary modifiers.

Prepare for the next round.

sections.title: Officer Activation
sections.body:
Each Officer activation consists of five phases.

Phase 1 — Activation

Spend CC.

Declare the Officer.

Confirm the Company being activated.

Phase 2 — Main Phase 1

Company AP may be spent for:

Movement outside Command Radius (Movement inside Command Radius is free)

Activated abilities

Positioning

Combat attacks may not occur during this phase.

Phase 3 — Combat Phase

Combat is divided into four steps.

Step 1 — Declare Attacks

The active player declares every attacking unit.

For each attacker declare:

Target

Attack Method

Damage assignment (if required)

Every attacking unit may perform one attack unless another rule states otherwise.

A unit may only use 1 activated offensive ability from itself.

Abilities may stack if other friendly units provide the ability.

Standard Attack

Attack one target.

Excess Damage is lost.

Cleave

When using Cleave:

You may divide this unit's Damage among up to as many targets as its Damage value (each target at least 1). Example — Damage 3: one target for 3; two for 2 and 1; or three for 1 each.

Declare every target and assignment before any Hit rolls.

Roll separately against every target.

Missed attacks lose their assigned Damage.

Cleave may be used by melee or ranged attacks if the card allows it.

Trample

Trample is a melee-only Attack Method.

When a Trample attack destroys an adjacent enemy:

Remaining Damage is retained.

The attacker may move into the defeated unit's hex.

If it does not move, Trample immediately ends.

If it moves, it may immediately attack another adjacent enemy using the remaining Damage.

A new Hit roll is made for every Trample attack.

The Trample chain ends when:

No Damage remains.

A Hit roll fails.

The attacking player chooses not to advance.

There are no adjacent enemy units.

MultiStrike

MultiStrike X

This attack makes X attacks against the same target.

Roll separately for each attack.

If the target is destroyed before all attacks are completed, any remaining attacks are lost.

Step 2 — Declare Defensive Reactions

After all attacks have been declared,

the defending player declares Defensive Reactions.

Each defending unit may declare one Defensive Reaction.

Examples include:

Brace

Evade

Retaliate

Each Defensive Reaction costs Company AP.

Step 3 — Resolve Attack Sequences

After all attacks and Defensive Reactions have been declared, the active player chooses the order in which attacking units resolve their attacks.

Each attacking unit resolves its entire Attack Sequence before another attacking unit begins resolving theirs.

Attack Sequence

An Attack Sequence includes every effect generated by a unit's declared attack, including:

Hit rolls

Damage

Defensive Reactions

Triggered abilities

Passive effects

Additional attacks generated by the attack

Movement generated by the attack

Only after the Attack Sequence has completely finished does the next attacking unit begin resolving its attack.

Example

Declared attacks:

Soldier attacks Wolf A.

Mammoth (Trample) attacks Wolf B.

The active player chooses to resolve the Mammoth first.

The Mammoth:

Hits Wolf B.

Destroys Wolf B.

Retains remaining Damage.

Moves into Wolf B's hex.

Attacks Wolf A.

Continues Trample until the chain ends.

Only after the Mammoth's entire Attack Sequence is complete does the Soldier resolve its attack.

If Wolf A has already been destroyed, the Soldier's attack is lost.

Step 4 — Combat Cleanup

After every Attack Sequence has resolved:

Remove destroyed units.

Resolve "after combat" abilities.

Resolve any remaining triggered effects.

Combat Phase then ends.

Phase 4 — Main Phase 2

Company AP may again be spent for:

Movement outside Command Radius (Movement inside Command Radius is free)

Activated abilities

Positioning

Combat attacks may not occur during this phase.

Phase 5 — End Phase

Resolve:

Isolated checks.

End-of-activation abilities.

Status duration changes.

sections.title: Movement
sections.body:
Each unit has a Movement value.

Movement is measured in hexes.

Movement may be split between Main Phase 1 and Main Phase 2.

Company AP Cost

Moving inside the Officer's Command Radius costs 0 Company AP.

Moving while outside the Officer's Command Radius costs Company AP (plus Isolated's +1 if applicable).

Terrain Costs

Non-water terrain has no movement penalty. All passable land (Plains, Forest, Swamp, Desert, Volcanic, Mountains) costs 1 Movement to enter.

Water remains impassable unless a unit has an ability that allows water movement.

Roads

The first time a unit enters a Road during an activation,

it gains

+1 Movement

for the remainder of that activation.

Favored Terrain

Units on their favored terrain gain that terrain's Favored bonus. Each race has a favored terrain type:

Human, Construct → Plains

Beastfolk, Elf → Forest

Dragon, Demon → Volcanic

Undead, Lizardman → Swamp

Dwarf → Mountains

Units may also gain Favored bonuses through terrain keywords (Open Ground, Woodwalker, Bogstrider, Duneborn, Ashborn, Mountainborn, Deepwalker) on the matching terrain type regardless of race.

Terrain Effects (Base / Favored)

Plains — Base: none. Favored: +1 Hit when attacking from Plains.

Forest — Base: Ranged attacks (Range 2+) against units in Forest suffer +1 Hit Requirement. Favored: While attacking from Forest, ignore that Forest Base penalty.

Mountains — Base: Attacks against units in Mountains suffer +1 Hit Requirement, unless the attacker is also in Mountains. Favored: While in Mountains, +1 Harden (stacks).

Swamp — Base: Flanking does not grant its bonus against a unit in Swamp unless the attacker is also in Swamp. Favored: While in Swamp, this unit has Guard.

Desert — Base: Units in Desert cannot use Evade. Favored: +1 Hit when attacking from Desert.

Volcanic — Base: Units in Volcanic cannot use Brace. Favored: +1 Damage when attacking from Volcanic.

Water — Base: Only Flying or Amphibious units may occupy Water. Favored: +1 Move while in Water.

Wall — Base: Impassable obstacle (see Walls). Favored: none.

Occupancy

Only one model may occupy a hex.

Friendly models may not share a hex.

Enemy models block movement.

Disengagement

Leaving adjacency with an enemy provokes a Disengagement Strike: that enemy may immediately perform one melee attack against the moving unit.

Alternatively, the moving unit may spend +1 Company AP before leaving adjacency to leave cleanly (no Strike).

Guard: If the enemy being left has Guard, the moving unit must take that unit's Disengagement Strike and cannot buy it off with +1 Company AP.

Harass: A Move granted by Harass (Move 1 after attacking) ignores Disengagement, including Guard.

sections.title: Combat
sections.body:
Combat is intentionally deterministic.

Damage is flat.

There is no Armor statistic.

Toughness determines survivability.

Hit Rolls

Roll 2d6. The attack hits if the sum is equal to or greater than the Hit Requirement.

Base Hit Requirement:

Apply modifiers after determining the base requirement. Final requirements are clamped between 5+ and 11+.

Damage

Successful attacks deal Damage equal to the attacker's current Damage.

Damage reduces Toughness.

If Toughness reaches zero, the unit is destroyed.

Excess Damage

Excess Damage is normally lost.

Only rules that explicitly state otherwise (such as Trample) may retain or redistribute excess Damage.

sections.title: Fortifications
sections.body:
A Fortification is a hex token that represents prepared defenses (barricades, earthworks, or held works).

Placing Fortifications

Effects that say Fortify place a Fortification on a hex.

A hex may have at most one Fortification.

Fortify does not move with a unit. If the unit leaves the hex, the Fortification remains.

Occupying a Fortified Hex

While a unit occupies a Fortified hex, it has Harden 1 (Piercing and melee Siege ignore Harden).

This Harden 1 stacks with printed Harden and other Harden sources.

Damage may never be reduced below 1.

Demolish

When declaring an attack against a Fortified hex, a unit with Siege (or another rule that allows Demolish) may choose one mode:

Attack the unit — Resolve combat normally. The occupant still benefits from the Fortification's Damage reduction.

Demolish the Fortification — Make a Hit roll using the normal Distance | Roll table against the occupant (or 7+ if the hex is empty). On a hit, remove the Fortification and deal no Damage to the unit unless the attacker's card says otherwise.

Siege Bonus

When a unit with Siege deals Damage to a unit on a Fortified hex (Attack the unit mode), increase that Damage by 1 unless the card states a higher bonus (for example +2).

Design intent: Fortifications reward holding bridges and objectives against infantry, while catapults and rams punish static bunkers.

Siege Units (movement)

Siege units are typically Move 2 — a step slower than most line infantry (Move 3+). Only Siege may print Move 2 (or lower). All other card types floor at Move 3.

Heavier engines may also have Slow, or rarely Move 1.

Abilities such as Limber Up, Haul Lines, and Tow Hitch exist to help Siege reposition without raising their printed Move.

sections.title: Walls
sections.body:
A Wall is a hex terrain token (Wall Segment or Wall Corner) that blocks occupation.

Occupation

No unit may occupy a Wall hex — including Flying units.

Gaps

Leave a hex without a Wall token to create a passage. There is no separate Gate piece.

Movement and Flying

Non-Flying units cannot enter a Wall hex.

Flying units may path across Wall hexes while moving (they fly over), but cannot end a move or otherwise occupy a Wall hex.

Demolish

Siege (and similar rules) may Demolish a Wall the same way they Demolish a Fortification: on a hit, remove that Wall token. Demolish targets one Wall hex at a time.

Walls vs Fortifications

Walls cannot be occupied.

Fortified outlines can be occupied; the occupant gains the Fortification benefits (see Fortifications).

Objectives

Wall tokens may not be placed on an objective hex (objectives are placed before terrain).

sections.title: Blast (Splash Damage)
sections.body:
Blast is used by Dragons and some Siege artillery (hurled shot / explosive payloads).

When a unit has Blast (or an effect grants Blast), choose a primary target and deal Damage to that target and each enemy within 1 hex of it (the six adjacent hexes). Blast does not scale to a larger radius.

Roll Hit separately against each enemy in the blast. A miss deals no Damage to that enemy.

Blast does not hit friendly units unless a card says so.

Blast is an Attack Method. It cannot be combined with Cleave or Trample in the same attack.

sections.title: Overpenetrate (Bolt-Through)
sections.body:
Overpenetrate is used by ballista-type Siege (bolts and greatbows), not hurled Blast shot.

If the primary target is destroyed, leftover Damage (printed Damage minus the target's Toughness before the hit) continues in a straight line behind them, away from the attacker. Empty hexes are skipped. The next enemy on that line takes a new Hit roll using the leftover Damage. Friendly units and commanders stop the bolt without taking Damage.

If that enemy is also destroyed, leftover Damage may continue along the same line.

Overpenetrate cannot be combined with Blast.

sections.title: Defensive Reactions
sections.body:
Each attacked unit may declare one Defensive Reaction.

Brace

Spend 1 Company AP.

This unit gains Harden 1 until its next activation or the next round, whichever comes first.

Brace Harden stacks with printed Harden and other Harden sources. Piercing and melee Siege ignore it.

Brace is a Defensive Reaction only. Abilities never grant Brace.

Evade

Spend 1 Company AP.

Attacks against this unit suffer +1 Hit Requirement.

Evade lasts until this unit's next activation or the next round, whichever comes first.

A unit may not have Brace and Evade at the same time.

Retaliate

Spend 1 Company AP.

Immediately perform a simultaneous counterattack following all normal combat rules.

A unit may Retaliate only once per round.

sections.title: Officer Death & Command Succession
sections.body:
The battlefield is built around maintaining a functioning command structure. Losing an Officer disrupts a Company but should not immediately cripple an army.

Officer Death

When an Officer is destroyed:

Remove the Officer from play immediately.

Remove all passive abilities and aura effects granted by that Officer.

The Company remains intact.

All Combat Units remain assigned to that Company.

The Company continues to generate no Company AP until a replacement Officer is promoted.

Temporary Promotion

A player may spend 1 CC to temporarily promote a Combat Unit within the Company.

Promotion may occur immediately after the Officer is destroyed or during any later point that player could normally spend CC.

The promoted unit becomes the Acting Officer.

Acting Officer

An Acting Officer gains:

Company AP generation.

A Command Radius.

The ability to activate the Company.

The ability to spend Company AP.

The Acting Officer does not gain the original Officer's card abilities.

The Acting Officer keeps:

Original Damage

Original Toughness

Original Passive abilities

Temporary Command Radius

Acting Officers use a reduced Command Radius.

Default Command Radius: 2 hexes

This value may be adjusted during future balancing.

Promotion Duration

Temporary promotions last 2 rounds.

At the end of the second round:

The Acting Officer returns to being a normal Combat Unit.

If another Officer has not joined the Company, the Company becomes leaderless again.

Re-Promotion

A Company may be promoted multiple times during a battle by spending additional CC.

Leaderless Companies

A Company without an Officer or Acting Officer:

Generates no Company AP.

Cannot activate as a Company.

Units remain assigned to that Company.

Units may only activate individually by spending CC as Isolated Units.

sections.title: Commander Death
sections.body:
Commanders represent the strategic leadership of an army.

Losing the Commander should be significant without immediately ending the game.

Commander Destroyed

When the Commander is destroyed:

Remove the Commander from play.

Immediately stop generating CC.

Commander passive abilities are lost.

Officer Companies continue functioning normally.

Existing Company AP

Existing Company AP remains.

Officers continue to activate using any remaining CC already generated that round.

Beginning the following round:

No additional CC is generated.

Strategic Collapse

Without a Commander:

Officers continue commanding Companies.

Company AP continues functioning normally.

No new CC is generated.

This creates increasing strategic pressure without immediately ending the game.

sections.title: Entity Authority
sections.body:
Whenever two rules conflict, resolve them using the following hierarchy.

Higher authority always overrides lower authority.

sections.title: Core Rules
sections.body: The Rulebook always takes precedence unless a card explicitly states it overrides a rule.

sections.title: Scenario Rules
sections.body: Scenario-specific rules override standard game rules.

sections.title: Commander Abilities
sections.body:
Commander abilities override:

Officer abilities

Unit abilities

unless another rule explicitly states otherwise.

sections.title: Officer Abilities
sections.body:
Officer abilities override Combat Unit abilities.

Officer effects only apply to Combat Units assigned to that Officer unless otherwise stated.

sections.title: Combat Unit Abilities
sections.body:
Combat Unit abilities affect only that unit unless otherwise stated. Friendly single-target heals and buffs on a Combat Unit may target any friendly creature within the ability''s Range (Combat Units, Officers, or Commanders). 
Whenever a specific rule conflicts with a general rule,

the specific rule always wins.

A unit may only activate 1 offensive ability during their attack.

A unit may gain activated effects from officers/commanders during their 

attack.  

Example:

General Rule

Units attack once.

Specific Ability

"This unit may attack twice."

The specific ability overrides the general rule.

Abilities Override Default Rules

Abilities that explicitly change combat override normal combat rules.

Examples:

Trample overrides:

Excess Damage is lost.

Adaptive Attack overrides:

Printed Damage value.

Future abilities follow the same principle.

sections.title: Rarity
sections.body:
Rarity represents a card's power budget and complexity.

It is not a collectible rarity.

Common

Black Gem

Generally has:

Lower UV

Few or no abilities

Straightforward battlefield role

Uncommon

Generally has:

Moderate UV

Generally has:

sections.title: Glossary
sections.body:
AP (Action Points): Tactical resource generated by Officers or Commanders and spent to perform actions.

Attack Sequence: All effects generated by a single declared attack, including Hit rolls, Damage, triggered abilities, movement, and additional attacks.

CC (Command Cost): Strategic resource generated by the Commander and spent on command-level actions.

Combat Unit: Any non-Officer, non-Commander unit assigned to a Company.

Command Radius: The area in which an Officer effectively commands their Company.

Company: A group of Combat Units assigned to a single Officer.

Company AP: The shared Action Point pool generated by an Officer and used by units within that Company. Attacks, reactions, and abilities spend Company AP. Movement spends Company AP only while outside Command Radius.

Company UV Capacity: The maximum total UV of Combat Units an Officer may command.

Damage: The amount of Toughness removed by a successful attack.

Demolish: An attack mode available to Siege (and similar rules) that removes a Fortification or Wall token on a hit (instead of damaging an occupying unit, when applicable).

Fortification / Fortified hex: An outline hex token. While occupied, the occupant has Harden 1 (Piercing and melee Siege ignore Harden). Placed by effects that Fortify or by Fortified terrain pieces. Passable — units may occupy it.

Objective: A scenario marker. Place via a drawn Objective Card (after Commanders, before terrain). Cards show 1–3 pre-balanced hexes aligned to the board grid. Water and Wall may not be placed on an objective hex. Objective hexes are always neutral land (Plains) for gameplay purposes — terrain may visually overlap but that hex remains passable. No Officer or Combat Unit may deploy within 5 hexes of an objective.

Objective Card: A setup card with a mini-map of 1, 2, or 3 objective locations and a center mark. Draw one from the deck; align card center to the board center reference and edges to N/W/S/E; place those markers. Optional roll to rotate/flip orientation (centers stay aligned).

Center reference: A marked mid-board hex used to align Objective Cards and read the map. Not an objective unless a card places one there.

Wall: A blocking hex terrain token. No unit may occupy it (including Flying). Flying may path across while moving but cannot end on it. Leave empty hexes for gaps. Siege may Demolish one Wall hex at a time. May not be placed on an objective hex.

Hit Requirement: The 2d6 sum needed for an attack to succeed.

Harden X: Printed keyword. Reduce incoming Damage by the sum of all Harden sources on the unit. Piercing ignores Harden. Melee Siege (Range 1 rams and similar engines) also ignore Harden. Always print the number (Harden 1, Harden 2, …). Harden sources stack.

Isolated: A unit outside its Officer's Command Radius. Isolated units still belong to their Company but pay +1 Company AP for every action and cannot benefit from Officer abilities. Movement only costs Company AP when outside Command Radius; Isolated's +1 still applies to that Move.

Officer: A unit that commands a Company, generates Company AP, and provides tactical leadership.

Range: Printed attack distance. Melee is Range 1. Printed Range never exceeds 3. Temporary +Range from Actives may raise effective Range above 3 for that activation only. Those Actives are primarily Elf (archery) or narrow Siege-elevation tools — not a shared toolbox for every race.

Siege (keyword): May Demolish Fortifications and Walls; deals +1 Damage (or more if printed) to units on Fortified hexes.

Toughness: A unit's health. When Toughness reaches 0, the unit is destroyed.

Favored Terrain: Each race has a favored terrain type (Human/Construct → Plains, Beastfolk/Elf → Forest, Dragon/Demon → Volcanic, Undead/Lizardman → Swamp, Dwarf → Mountains). Favored bonuses are terrain-specific (see Terrain Effects). Units may also gain Favored via terrain keywords.

Terrain Keywords: Keywords that grant favored terrain bonuses regardless of race: Open Ground (Plains), Woodwalker (Forest), Bogstrider (Swamp), Duneborn (Desert), Ashborn (Volcanic), Mountainborn (Mountains), Deepwalker (Water).

Unit Value (UV): The point value used when constructing armies.

sections.title: Table: Terrain Types
sections.body:
Terrain | Movement Cost | Notes

Plains | 1 | Favored by Human, Construct. Favored: +1 Hit from Plains.

Forest | 1 | Favored by Beastfolk, Elf. Base: ranged into Forest +1 Hit Requirement. Favored: ignore that penalty when attacking from Forest.

Swamp | 1 | Favored by Undead, Lizardman. Base: Flanking does not apply unless attacker also in Swamp. Favored: Guard while in Swamp.

Desert | 1 | Favored by none (keyword: Duneborn). Base: cannot use Evade. Favored: +1 Hit from Desert.

Volcanic | 1 | Favored by Dragon, Demon. Base: cannot use Brace. Favored: +1 Damage from Volcanic.

Mountains | 1 | Favored by Dwarf. Base: +1 Hit Requirement vs units here unless attacker also in Mountains. Favored: +1 Harden while in Mountains (stacks).

Water | Impassable | Unless Flying or Amphibious. Favored (Deepwalker): +1 Move while in Water.

Wall | Impassable | Blocks occupation; Flying may path over but not end on. No Favored bonus.

Road | 1 | First entry grants +1 Movement for activation

Favored Terrain Bonus: Terrain-specific (see Terrain Effects under Movement).

Terrain Keywords: Open Ground (Plains), Woodwalker (Forest), Bogstrider (Swamp), Duneborn (Desert), Ashborn (Volcanic), Mountainborn (Mountains), Deepwalker (Water) grant that terrain's Favored bonus regardless of race.
